 The Washington Capitals (10-8-0) and Tampa Bay Lightning (13-5-2) will meet in the NHL tonight. Puck drop is set for 7:30 p.m. EST at Benchmark International Arena in Tampa, Fla. The game will be broadcast live on ESPN+.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Lightning are favored at -160 on the moneyline, with the Capitals at +132 to pull off the upset. The over/under is set at 6.5 (-105o / -115u).
 Let's get into our Capitals vs. Lightning predictions and NHL picks .
 Capitals vs. Lightning Prediction
 Pick: Over 6.5 Goals (-105, FanDuel | Play to -110) 
 Our Washington vs. Tampa Bay best bet is on the over total goals, with the best odds currently available at FanDuel. For all of your NHL bets, be sure to find the best lines by using our live NHL odds page. 
 Capitals vs Lightning Odds
 Capitals vs. Lightning puck line: Capitals +1.5 (-176), Lightning -1.5 (+142)
 Capitals vs. Lightning over/under: 6.5 (-105o / -115u)
 Capitals vs. Lightning moneyline: Capitals +132, Lightning -160
 Capitals vs. Lightning best bet: Over 6.5
 The Capitals have had a difficult time containing high-quality offensive opposition of late, with several of the league's better offensive teams exposing their shaky defensive-zone structure. Washington possesses legitimate offensive upside across all four lines but has far too often needed to score its way out of trouble this season.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Jakob Chychrun and Cole Hutson offer significant offensive upside from the back end, but both have been shaky defensively, with Hutson in particular struggling in his own zone. Aside from the presence of Vezina-caliber netminder Logan Thompson in goal, the strengths and weaknesses of Washington's personnel suggest that it should continue to play in a lot of high-scoring matchups.
 The Capitals have allowed 3.66 xGA/60 this season, which is the third-worst mark in the NHL. As expected, the Lightning have been one of the league's most productive sides, generating 3.70 goals per game thus far.
 Washington has faced five straight matchups against some of the league's stronger defensive sides (Dallas, Florida, New Jersey twice, and Ottawa), yet still averaged 3.6 goals per game over that span. The Capitals have the offensive upside to generate chances against any opponent.
 At -105, there looks to be value backing this exciting matchup to feature over 6.5 goals.
